    def is_point_inside_another_black_sheet(px, py):

    # Check a few critical points on the table to see if they can be seen from above
    test_points = [
        (x1 - 0.5, y1 - 0.5),  # Bottom-left of table

        (x1 - 0.5, y2 + 0.5),  # Top-left of table
        (x2 + 0.5, y2 + 0.5),  # Top-right of table
        (x3, y3),              # Bottom-left of first black sheet
        (x4, y4),              # Top-right of first black sheet
        (x5, y5),              # Bottom-left of second black sheet
        (x6, y6),              # Top-right of second black sheet
        ((x1 + x2) / 2, (y1 + y2) / 2)  # Center of white sheet
    ]
    
    for point in test_points:

           not is_point_inside_black_sheet(px, py) and \

def can_white_sheet_be_seen(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, x4, y4, x5, y5, x6, y6):
    # Check if there is any point not strictly inside the white sheet and outside both black sheets

    def is_inside(px, py, rx1, ry1, rx2, ry2):
        return rx1 < px < rx2 and ry1 < py < ry2

    # Helper function to determine if a point is on the boundary of a rectangle
    def is_on_boundary(px, py, rx1, ry1, rx2, ry2):
        return (rx1 <= px <= rx2 and (py == ry1 or py == ry2)) or \
               (ry1 <= py <= ry2 and (px == rx1 or px == rx2))

    # Check white sheet's boundary points

        (x1, y1), (x1, y2), (x2, y1), (x2, y2)
    ]

    for px, py in boundary_points:
        if not is_inside(px, py, x3, y3, x4, y4) and not is_inside(px, py, x5, y5, x6, y6) and \
           not is_on_boundary(px, py, x3, y3, x4, y4) and not is_on_boundary(px, py, x5, y5, x6, y6):
            return "YES"

    # Check interior points of the white sheet

        ((x1 + x2) / 2, (y1 + y2) / 2),  # center
